added_failures_note: The reviewed run's record carries no baseline_suite and no after_suite (its manifest declares the suite unarmed), so no added failure can be derived from a suite pair; its own gate log (gate.log) records 26 passed with EXIT=0 and its negative-control log records 8 failed with EXIT=1.

findings.text: A comment the caller supplied as a `#SBATCH --comment=` directive in a submitted script is not kept: the wrapper built at reckon/nested_launch.py:940-942 carries the script's directive, but the `--comment=` prepended at :1049 is a command-line option and overrides it, so the evidence fragment's claim that a caller's comment is preserved holds only for an argv-supplied comment.

Every comment case hands the shim RECKON_SESSION_ID itself (tests/test_a_scheduler_job_names_its_owner.py:103-104), so the suite passes whatever the dispatcher does; removing the export at reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:1211 leaves all twelve cases green and the shipped behaviour dead, and the export half needs its own assertion.

owner_comment returns nothing without a run id, so a scheduler job reckon submits on behalf of a coordinator with a session but no run (reckon/crew/placement.py:1199, reckon/crew/landing_measure.py:882) still names no owner, against the deliverable's "or by reckon itself" clause.

find_allocations identifies a fleet allocation by exact comment equality, so an owner appended to a fleet submission's comment would make that allocation invisible to the fleet readers; no current caller both carries a run id and submits the fleet, so the append makes an unsafe combination reachable rather than breaking a live path.
